cards.explanation: The answer is that there is no one like the LORD in all the earth. The LORD says it plainly: "…so you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth." (Exodus 9:14) The plagues are not just trouble for Egypt. They are showing Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who the LORD is.

The answer is power. The LORD says, "But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth." (Exodus 9:16) Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is about to see it up close, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD tells Pharaoh, "Still, you lord it over My people and do not allow them to go." (Exodus 9:17) That word "still" says Pharaoh hasn't budged, friends.

The answer is to shelter the livestock and everything in the field. The LORD says, "So give orders now to shelter your livestock and everything you have in the field." (Exodus 9:19) Pharaoh, king of Egypt, gets a plan along with the warning.

The answer is True, and the LORD says it straight. "Every man or beast that remains in the field and is not brought inside will die when the hail comes down upon them." (Exodus 9:19) It's a heavy line, friends. The warning comes before the hail, and it begins with the LORD telling Pharaoh to give orders now to shelter his livestock and everything in the field.

The answer is whether they feared the word of the LORD. Some officials "…feared the word of the LORD…" and hurried to shelter their servants and livestock, while "…those who disregarded the word of the LORD…" left them in the field (Exodus 9:20-21). Same warning, two responses, friends.

The answer is thunder and lightning, friends! The sky went full drum solo with a light show on top. The text says, "The hail fell and the lightning continued flashing through it." (Exodus 9:24) Moses only stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sent the rest.

The answer is False. The hail did not leave the trees alone. The text says it "…beat down every plant of the field and stripped every tree." (Exodus 9:25) The trees took the hit with everything else, friends.

The answer is the land of Goshen. "The only place where it did not hail was in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived." (Exodus 9:26) The hail struck down everything in the field throughout the land of Egypt (Exodus 9:25). Goshen was the one place it did not touch, friends.

The answer is that the LORD is righteous. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, says, "This time I have sinned…" and then, "The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked." (Exodus 9:27) Those are big words from him. The next verses show what he does after the storm.

The answer is that Pharaoh asks Moses and Aaron to pray to the LORD. He says, "Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail." (Exodus 9:28) He wants the storm to end. He adds, "I will let you go…" and asks them to speak to the LORD about it, friends.
The answer is the LORD. Moses says the thunder will cease and the hail will stop "…so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s." (Exodus 9:29) The whole earth, friends, not just Goshen.

The answer is False. Moses tells Pharaoh, "But as for you and your officials, I know that you still do not fear the LORD our God." (Exodus 9:30) Pharaoh had just said, "The LORD is righteous…" yet Moses says they still do not fear the LORD. The word "still" is the key, friends.

The answer is True. The text says "…the wheat and spelt were not destroyed, because they are late crops." (Exodus 9:32) The barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom, so those were destroyed (Exodus 9:31). The crop's timing made the difference, friends.

The answer is that he sins again and hardens his heart. "When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had ceased, he sinned again and hardened his heart…" (Exodus 9:34) Only a few verses earlier he had said, "I will let you go…" (Exodus 9:28). The storm ended and so did his promise, friends.

The answer is True. The text says Pharaoh sinned again and hardened his heart, and his officials did too (Exodus 9:34). The officials joined him, friends. The passage then says Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he would not let the Israelites go (Exodus 9:35).
